Living Well / Free resources

Nature, science & everyday wonder

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Explore a familiar bird, the night sky, an ocean question, or a hands-on explanation of something you have noticed.

Wonder does not need an exotic setting. An unfamiliar sound, a shadow, or a question about water can open a satisfying line of inquiry. This collection brings together observation aids, scientific explanations, and visual tools that help curiosity move beyond the screen.

Start with: All About Birds: bird guide. Look up a familiar bird and compare its description with what you noticed.

App · Free core app

Merlin Bird ID

Cornell Lab of Ornithology

A small way to connect an unfamiliar bird with a question you can investigate. The identification is the beginning of noticing, not the end.

Begin here: Read the official setup guide and check the identification support for your region.

Access: Free app; email confirmation is required for continued use. Download only through the official links.

Perspective: Nature-identification tool

Merlin setup and access guide

Context & source

Suggestions can be wrong, and Sound ID coverage varies by region. No credit card is required by Merlin.

App · Free core app

Seek by iNaturalist

iNaturalist

Image recognition can help you ask better questions about something already nearby, rather than give you another reason to keep scrolling.

Begin here: Read about the app before installing. Try observing one thing without needing to collect badges.

Access: Free app; no registration required for basic use.

Perspective: Nature-identification tool

Learn about Seek

Context & source

Optional iNaturalist sign-in and posting change data sharing. Never use identification guesses to decide what is safe to eat or touch.

Borrow something with Libby

OverDrive and participating libraries

Sometimes the most useful technology simply gets a book into reach. There is no need to turn reading into a course or a reading challenge.

Begin here: Find your library and browse what is available before choosing a title. The web version is an option on supported browsers.

Access: Free borrowing with an eligible card at a participating library. Titles and waits vary by library.

Perspective: Public-library borrowing

Interactive sky map · Free browser interactive

Stellarium Web

Stellarium Labs

An example of a focused digital tool supporting an ordinary question about the sky rather than demanding prolonged attention.

Begin here: Explore the map for a chosen location and time; check the settings before interpreting it.

Access: Free browser star map. JavaScript is required; desktop and mobile products have separate offerings.

Perspective: Astronomical visualization

Explore Stellarium Web

Context & source

A simulation is not a weather report or a guarantee of visibility. Never look at the Sun through unfiltered optics.

Keep the context

Take what is useful, thoughtfully.

Use identification and visualization tools as learning aids, not as guarantees about the world in front of you. Keep safe distances from wildlife, do not use an identification guess to decide what to eat, and follow activity-specific safety instructions. A text explanation or an indoor observation is just as valid a route as an outing.

Selections are based on public source review, not a claim that Nolan uses every resource or belongs to the organizations listed.
